In 2024, PV generated approximately 7% of U.S. electricity and—after years of being the leading source of new U.S. generation capacity—was the second largest source of capacity, representing tens of billions of dollars of products within a variety of supply chains (Figure 1). At the end of 2024, the United States had a cumulative PV capacity of 224.1 GW direct current (GW ), with 47.1 GW of PV installed in 2024 alone. dc dc Figure 1. PV systems provide electricity when the sun is up, but production wanes around the hours of peak demand in some parts of the country, typically 4–7 p.m. across U.S. time zones. Short-term battery energy storage systems (BESS) can help meet demand in those later hours, charging with PV-generated electricity from morning to late afternoon and then, most commonly, discharging over a period of 1–6 hours. BESS use has been growing with the help of falling lithium-ion battery (LIB) cell and system costs. From 2020 to 2024, U.S. BESS installations grew more than tenfold, with a year-end cumulative capacity of 96.0 GWh (33.6 GW ), including 31.1 GWh ac (12.3 GW ) installed in 2024 (Masson, Van Rechem, et al. 2025). Together, PV and BESS ac represented more than 65% of new U.S. electricity capacity additions in 2023 and 84% in 2024. Figure 2 shows annual U.S. PV installations from 2010 to 2024 across the utility-scale sector and the two distributed sectors: nonresidential (commercial and industrial applications, carports, schools, etc.) and residential. Utility-scale systems have accounted for most U.S. PV installations, with a compound annual growth rate of 35%. Annual U.S. PV additions, 2010–2024 As PV and BESS have grown in importance, they have increasingly become subject to federal policies and trade actions aimed, at least in part, at supporting U.S. manufacturing (Figure 3). From 2009 to 2012, the average global price of PV modules dropped by around 30% per year owing to the rapid expansion of low-cost Chinese production. The U.S. PV industry, which had been operating around trade parity before 2010, began importing more Chinese modules to meet growing demand.
